issues.title: feat: Remove single-security-group enforcement from UI and controller
issues.description:
Two enforcement layers prevent a user from being assigned more than one security group per organization, even though the data model and service layer already support it. The client-side JavaScript in \_EditHelper.cshtml converts the checkbox group into a radio-button-like widget that unchecks siblings on selection (lines 136–155). UserController.cs independently rejects saves when `viewModel.Groups.Ids.Count() > 1` (lines 93–96 in `Create`, lines 171–174 in `Edit`). Both must be removed; no database or service changes are needed.

**Files to modify:**

* Source/OneNListApp.Web/Areas/Admin/Views/User/\_EditHelper.cshtml — delete the `checkboxes.forEach` change listener (lines 136–155) that unchecks sibling checkboxes when one is selected
* Source/OneNListApp.Web/Areas/Admin/Controllers/UserController.cs — remove the `if (viewModel.Groups.Ids.Count() > 1)` `ModelState.AddModelError` block in both `Create` (line 93) and `Edit` (line 171)

**Acceptance Criteria:**

*  An admin can check multiple security group checkboxes simultaneously on the create/edit user form; checking one does not uncheck the others
*  Saving a user with two or more security groups selected does not produce a validation error
*  Project builds with no errors or warnings after the change
*  All existing tests continue to pass

**Unit Test Requirements:**

* `UserController.Edit_MultipleGroupsSelected_SavesWithoutValidationError` — passes two group IDs in `viewModel.Groups.Ids`; asserts no `ModelState` error is added and `UpdateByIdsAsync` is called with both IDs

issues.title: feat: Update session layer to store and propagate multiple security group IDs
issues.description:
`SessionUserData` holds a single `int? SecurityGroupId` field, and `SessionController.LoadUserPermissions` reads only the first row from `Organization_Security_Config` via `.FirstOrDefault()` (line 278), silently dropping any additional group assignments. These must be updated so that all group IDs for the authenticated organization are collected, serialized as a comma-separated claim, and deserialized back into `List<int> SecurityGroupIds` on subsequent reads. All callers of the singular `SessionManager.GetSecurityGroupId()` must be audited and updated to work with the list.

**Files to modify:**

* Source/OneNListApp.Web/Helpers/SessionUserData.cs — replace `int? SecurityGroup` (line 31) and `int? SecurityGroupId` (line 37) with a single `List<int> SecurityGroupIds { get; set; }` property
* Source/OneNListApp.Web/Helpers/SessionManager.cs — update `GetUserData()` (line 107) to read the `SecurityGroupIds` claim and split on `','` into a `List<int>`; update `SetSessionValue` calls (lines 296–297) to write the joined list; audit `userSecurityGroup()` (line 135) which returns a single enum value and update any callers that need a list variant
* Source/OneNListApp.Web/Controllers/SessionController.cs — in `LoadUserPermissions` (line 278), replace the `.FirstOrDefault()?.fk_SecurityGroup_ID` lookup with `.Where(x => x.fk_Organization_ID == organizationId).Select(x => x.fk_SecurityGroup_ID).Where(id => id.HasValue).Select(id => id!.Value).ToList()`; serialize the list to comma-separated when writing the `SecurityGroupIds` claim (lines 298–309); apply the same fix to the login path (line 115) and test-mode login path (line 226)

**Acceptance Criteria:**

*  A user assigned to two security groups in `Organization_Security_Config` gets both group IDs in their claims after login
*  `SessionManager.GetUserData()` correctly deserializes the comma-separated claim back to `List<int> SecurityGroupIds`
*  Single-group users are unaffected: their claim contains a one-element list and all downstream behavior is unchanged
*  All callers of the former singular `GetSecurityGroupId()` are updated or have an explicit comment explaining why the first-group fallback is still correct for that call site
*  Project builds with no errors or warnings after the change
*  All existing tests continue to pass

**Unit Test Requirements:**

* `SessionController.LoadUserPermissions_UserHasMultipleGroups_AllGroupIdsStoredInClaims` — mocks an `Organization_Security_Config` with two rows for the same user/org; asserts the resulting claim contains both IDs
* `SessionController.LoadUserPermissions_UserHasSingleGroup_SingleGroupIdInClaim` — regression guard: single-group user gets a one-element comma-separated claim

issues.title: feat: Refactor permission TVFs to union record visibility across all assigned security groups
issues.description:
`fnGetOneNListIDsUserHasPermissionsFor` and `BO_fnGetOneNListUserHasPermissionsFor` each resolve a single `@securityGroupId` scalar from `Organization_Security_Config` (migration `07_20260410_Fix_ACC_duplicate_rows_in_permission_TVFs.sql`, lines 80–94), so a user assigned to multiple groups only sees records visible to whichever row was returned first. Both functions must be refactored to load all of the user's group IDs into a table variable and `UNION` the permitted record sets across every group, giving the user the union of visibility across all assignments. The migration must also include an `IF EXISTS` guard to drop any unique constraint on `(fk_User_ID, fk_Organization_ID)` in `Organization_Security_Group` if one is present.

**Files to modify:**

* `Source/Migrations/<next-seq>_20260421_RefactorPermissionTVFsForMultipleSecurityGroups.sql` — new migration containing:
  * `ALTER FUNCTION dbo.fnGetOneNListIDsUserHasPermissionsFor`: replace the single `@securityGroupId` scalar with `DECLARE @groupIds TABLE (id INT); INSERT INTO @groupIds SELECT fk_SecurityGroup_ID FROM Organization_Security_Config WHERE fk_User_ID = @userId AND fk_Organization_ID = @organizationId AND fk_SecurityGroup_ID IS NOT NULL`; refactor each PM/Region/BO permission branch to `UNION` (deduplicated) results across all rows in `@groupIds`
  * `ALTER FUNCTION dbo.BO_fnGetOneNListUserHasPermissionsFor`: apply the identical table-variable-and-union pattern to maintain BI report parity
  * `IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.key_constraints kc JOIN sys.tables t ON kc.parent_object_id = t.object_id WHERE t.name = 'Organization_Security_Group' AND kc.type = 'UQ' AND ...)` guard to drop any unique constraint on `(fk_User_ID, fk_Organization_ID)` in that table

**Acceptance Criteria:**

*  A user assigned to two security groups sees the union of all records either group would individually grant — no record visible under group A or group B is absent from the combined result
*  A user assigned to one security group sees the same records as before (no regression)
*  `BO_fnGetOneNListUserHasPermissionsFor` returns a matching union result for equivalent inputs
*  If a unique constraint on `(fk_User_ID, fk_Organization_ID)` in `Organization_Security_Group` existed, the migration drops it cleanly
*  The migration runs without errors in the test environment
*  Project builds with no errors or warnings after the change
*  All existing tests continue to pass

issues.title: chore: Reassign Central Crestline Fleet Ops actions from PM TS to PM SAI
issues.description:
## Summary

Central Crestline has requested that all actions currently assigned to PM **"PD"** with PdM/PdD **"PD Fleet Ops"** be reassigned to PM **"SAI"**. The PdM/PdD lookup ("PD Fleet Ops") has already been re-parented from PM "PD" to PM "SAI" via the admin lookup tools, so `fk_PdMPdD_Lookup_ID` on `OneNList` does not change — only `fk_PMPD_Lookup_ID` is updated. Scoped to OrgID=2 (Central Crestline / Beacon).

The migration is delivered as an idempotent SQL script that resolves source and target LookupItem IDs by name (not hardcoded), previews the affected rows, and executes inside a transaction with explicit COMMIT/ROLLBACK.

## Files to Create

- `Source/Migrations/5.1.2/07_20260504_ReassignAerostatsActions_DataAnalytics.sql`

## Script Logic

### Step 1 — Resolve LookupItem IDs by name (OrgID=2)

PM lookups are org-scoped via `LookupItem_PMPDExt` → `Organization_Security_Group`. PdM/PdD lookups have no extension table, so they resolve by name; `parentId = @targetPmId` disambiguates "PD Fleet Ops" if the same name exists across orgs.

```sql
DECLARE @sourcePmId INT, @targetPmId INT, @pdAerostatsPdmId INT;

-- PM "PD"
SELECT @sourcePmId = li.ID
FROM [dbo].[LookupItem] li
INNER JOIN [dbo].[LookupItem_PMPDExt] pmext ON pmext.fk_LookupItem_ID = li.ID
INNER JOIN [dbo].[Organization_Security_Group] osg ON osg.ID = pmext.fk_PMSecurityGroupID
WHERE li.LookupItemValue = 'PD' AND osg.fk_Organization_ID = 2;

-- PM "SAI"
SELECT @targetPmId = li.ID
FROM [dbo].[LookupItem] li
INNER JOIN [dbo].[LookupItem_PMPDExt] pmext ON pmext.fk_LookupItem_ID = li.ID
INNER JOIN [dbo].[Organization_Security_Group] osg ON osg.ID = pmext.fk_PMSecurityGroupID
WHERE li.LookupItemValue = 'SAI' AND osg.fk_Organization_ID = 2;

-- PdM/PdD "PD Fleet Ops" (re-parented to PM "SAI")
SELECT @pdAerostatsPdmId = li.ID
FROM [dbo].[LookupItem] li
WHERE li.LookupItemValue = 'PD Fleet Ops' AND li.parentId = @targetPmId;
```

### Step 2 — Guards
RAISERROR + RETURN if any of the three IDs is NULL.

### Step 3 — Preview
```sql
SELECT o.ID, o.Title, o.fk_OrganizationId,
       pm.LookupItemValue AS CurrentPM, pdm.LookupItemValue AS CurrentPdMPdD
FROM [dbo].[OneNList] o
INNER JOIN [dbo].[LookupItem] pm  ON pm.ID  = o.fk_PMPD_Lookup_ID
INNER JOIN [dbo].[LookupItem] pdm ON pdm.ID = o.fk_PdMPdD_Lookup_ID
WHERE o.fk_PMPD_Lookup_ID    = @sourcePmId
  AND o.fk_PdMPdD_Lookup_ID  = @pdAerostatsPdmId
  AND o.fk_OrganizationId    = 2;
```

### Step 4 — Execute UPDATE in transaction
```sql
BEGIN TRANSACTION;
UPDATE [dbo].[OneNList]
SET fk_PMPD_Lookup_ID = @targetPmId,
    ModifiedBy        = SUSER_NAME(),
    ModifiedDate      = GETDATE()
WHERE fk_PMPD_Lookup_ID    = @sourcePmId
  AND fk_PdMPdD_Lookup_ID  = @pdAerostatsPdmId
  AND fk_OrganizationId    = 2;
SELECT @@ROWCOUNT AS RowsUpdated;
-- COMMIT;  ← uncomment to apply
-- ROLLBACK; ← uncomment to abort
```

### Step 5 — Verify (after COMMIT)
```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS StillOnSource
FROM [dbo].[OneNList]
WHERE fk_PMPD_Lookup_ID    = @sourcePmId
  AND fk_PdMPdD_Lookup_ID  = @pdAerostatsPdmId
  AND fk_OrganizationId    = 2;
-- Expected: 0
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Script resolves source PM ("PD"), target PM ("SAI"), and PdM/PdD ("PD Fleet Ops") IDs dynamically by name
- [ ] Guard clauses prevent execution if any name does not resolve
- [ ] Preview lists every action where PM="PD" AND PdM/PdD="PD Fleet Ops" for OrgID=2
- [ ] After COMMIT, those actions have PM="SAI", PdM/PdD value unchanged on `OneNList`
- [ ] After COMMIT, zero actions match the (PM="PD", PdM/PdD="PD Fleet Ops") pair for OrgID=2
- [ ] Script is idempotent — re-running after COMMIT updates 0 rows
- [ ] No app code changes; all existing unit tests continue to pass
